entries: When one of these pieces of Alchemical Ammunition hits, it deals the ammunition's normal damage, then applies the effect of the listed item to the target. No saving throw is allowed against this effect.

name: Sling Bullet, Incendiary
entries: When you hit with Incendiary ammunition, the target takes an additional {@damage 1d4} Fire damage.

name: Sling Bullet, Piercing
entries: Advanced Ammunition named after a damage type deals that damage type. Arrows and bolts can have wide heads that deal Slashing damage or blunt tips that deal Bludgeoning damage. A sling bullet can have facets that deal Piercing damage. All such ammo is heavier than normal; the weapon's maximum range while using it is halved.

name: Sling Bullet, Ranging
entries: Advanced Ammunition that has the Ranging property is lighter and better made than common counterparts. When you fire Ranging ammo, you can increase your weapon's normal range by 50 percent.

name: Sling Bullet, War Oil
entries: Alchemical Ammunition carries an alchemical payload. Rather than hurling a vial, you fire Alchemical Ammunition from a Ranged weapon, using your normal attack bonus with that weapon.
Alchemical Ammunition is heavier than normal; the weapon's normal and long ranges are halved. The Alchemical Ammunition is destroyed once used, whether the attack hits or misses.

entries.name: War Oil
entries: A target hit by a piece of Alchemical Ammunition packed with War Oil takes damage as normal for the ammunition, then becomes coated in War Oil for up to 1 minute. Alternatively, you can target a point, such as the ground or a wall, and on an attack roll against AC 10, cause the War Oil to spill out of the ammunition, creating a circular patch of the viscous substance with a 10-foot radius.

War Oil is slick and highly flammable. An area coated in War Oil counts as {@variantrule Difficult Terrain|XPHB}, and a creature that starting its turn in a coated area or enters the coated area for the first time on a turn must succeed a DC 10 Dexterity saving throw or gain the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition and have its {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} reduced to 0 until the end of its turn. Additionally, if a creature or area coated with War

Oil is exposed to an open flame or some other source of Fire damage, the oil ignites. The ignited oil burns for two rounds, dealing {@damage 2d4} Fire damage to any creature or object who comes in contact with it, and an additional {@damage 2d4} Fire damage to any creature that ends its turn while in contact with it. An ignited creature can douse the flames by using an action.
After burning for two rounds, being doused, or remaining unlit for 1 minute, War Oil dries up and ceases to be slippery or flammable.

name: Sling Bullet, Whistling
entries: Ammunition with the Whistling property creates a high-pitched sound after firing. This sound is audible out to 300 feet from the ammo as it flies. Whistling ammo isn't heavier, but it catches the air with intricate baffles to create its sound, so its maximum range is half normal. Whistling ammo deals Bludgeoning damage.

name: Smoke Bomb
entries: As a {@action Utilize|XPHB} action, you can throw this smoky glass vial to a space up to 30 feet away. When the vial breaks, the concoction creates a 10-foot-radius {@variantrule Sphere [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Sphere} of smoke. The area is {@variantrule Heavily Obscured|XPHB}. The smoke lasts for {@dice 1d4 + 2} rounds, or half as long in a windy area.

name: Stitching Needle
entries: This black iron needle easily pierces the skin. If a creature's mouth is sewn shut with a Stitching Needle, it loses the ability to speak and cast spells with verbal components. The creature gains the ability to communicate with {@variantrule Telepathy|XPHB} out to a range of 60 feet.
Stitching the mouth of a willing, {@condition Unconscious|XPHB}, or {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB} creature takes 10 minutes. Removing the stitches takes 1 minute.

name: Tower Shield
entries: This large shield provides more protection than a typical shield. While wielding a Tower Shield, you gain +3 to {@variantrule Armor Class|XPHB}. If you use an action to set the Tower Shield, you have {@variantrule Cover|XPHB|Three-Quarters Cover} until the start of your next turn. Additionally, your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} becomes 0 and cannot be increased during that time.
To wield a Tower Shield, you must have a Strength of at least 15 and your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} is reduced by 10 feet while wielding the shield.

name: Watcher's Candle
entries: This black tapered candle cannot be lit. When a Celestial, Fey, Fiend, or Undead comes within 120 feet of the candle, its wick ignites and burns with a purple flame. Once the candle has ignited, it burns for one hour, and it cannot be used again. Watcher's Candles cannot function if they are wrapped in packaging or stowed in a container.

name: Periapt of Proof against Poison and Paralysis
reprintedAs: Periapt of Proof against Poison and Petrified|GrimHollowMG24
entries: {@note This item has been created from Salvage text in the book; it may not be exactly as the author envisioned, some information is assumed.}

Someone who has proficiency with {@item alchemist's supplies|PHB} can take four lupilisk venom fangs, or just the two fangs of one lupilisk elder, and treat them with reagents worth 250 gp per tooth for 3 days. A successful treatment requires the alchemist to succeed on a {@dc 15} Intelligence or Wisdom check. During the treatment time, somebody must also cast {@spell lesser restoration} on the fangs. After a successful treatment, someone who has proficiency with {@item jeweler's tools|PHB} can fashion the fangs, now blackened, into a necklace, creating a {@item periapt of proof against poison and Paralysis|GHMG|periapt of proof against poison}. If the wearer attunes to the periapt, the amulet also provides that wearer immunity to being {@condition petrified}.

This delicate silver chain has a brilliant-cut black gem pendant. While you wear it, poisons have no effect on you. You are immune to the {@condition poisoned} condition and have immunity to poison damage.

name: Adamantine Polish
entries: This abrasive paste can be applied as an action to the claws, fangs, tusks, or spines of a creature to make them sharper, harder, or cleaner. For 8 hours after application, that creature gains a +1 to attack and damage rolls with its natural weapons, which count as being made of adamantine for the purposes of overcoming damage resistance and immunity.

name: Alchemical Anesthetic
entries: This clear, odorless potion is housed in a wickedlooking syringe which contains 4 doses. You can administer the anesthetic to a willing creature as an action, dulling its nerves and making it impossible for them to feel pain for one hour. An anesthetized creature has advantage on Constitution checks and saving throws and can't be {@condition incapacitated} or have disadvantage on rolls due to being in pain. However, the creature is unaware of how much pain they are in or how many levels of {@condition exhaustion} they have. If a player character is anesthetized, the GM tracks the character's hit points and levels of {@condition exhaustion} instead of the player for the duration.
If you administer a dose over the course of a minute to a willing or {@condition unconscious} creature, you can render the creature {@condition unconscious} for one hour.

If you continue to slowly administer anesthetic (one dose every eight hours), you can keep a creature {@condition unconscious} for up to 24 hours; keeping a creature {@condition unconscious} longer than this results in death.

name: Alchemical Reactor
entries: This stupendously complex vessel the size of a cask is festooned with valves and dials. While attuned to the reactor, you can use an action to adjust its settings and begin producing any of the following potions: {@item potion of flying}, {@item potion of hill giant strength}, {@item potion of invisibility}, {@item potion of superior healing}, {@item sovereign glue} (1 ounce), or {@item universal solvent}.

The reactor rumbles and whirs for the next 12 hours as it produces the specified potion. Once it is finished, you can use your action to pour the potion from the top of the reactor. This potion loses its potency and becomes nonmagical if it is not consumed within 24 hours.
Additionally, while attuned to the reactor, you can regain 2 expended reagent dice whenever you finish a short rest.

name: Ankh of Anubis
entries: While attuned to this wrought iron {@item holy symbol|PHB}, you have advantage on attack rolls, ability checks, and saving throws while you have 10 hit points or less.

Additionally, whenever you take damage, record the damage you take in a damage pool, which resets to 0 at the end of your turn. When you lose hit points to cast a martyr spell, you subtract the number in the damage pool from the spell's hit point cost, to a minimum of 0 hit points lost.

name: Antimagic Bell
entries: This round bell is enchanted to be perfectly silent.
It only rings when its magic is disrupted, such as within an {@spell antimagic field}.

name: Aqua Fortis
entries: This transparent acid constantly bubbles within its sealed vial. As an action, you can throw the vial up to 20 feet, shattering it on impact. Make a ranged attack, treating the vial as an improvised weapon. If the target is an object that isn't being worn or carried, the acid dissolves a 1-foot cube of the object. If splashed on a suit of armor or a shield, the object takes a permanent and cumulative -1 penalty to the AC it offers. A suit of armor reduced to an AC of 10 or a shield that drops to a +0 bonus is destroyed. If splashed on a weapon, it takes a permanent and cumulative -1 penalty to damage rolls. A weapon reduced to a -5 penalty is destroyed. It has no effect on magic items and objects made of gold, glass, stone, or adamantine.

If the target is a creature, it takes {@damage 3d6} acid damage, followed by an extra {@damage 2d6} acid damage at the end of its next turn and another {@damage 1d6} acid damage at the end of the turn after that. The acid can be washed off with one gallon of water, ending the effect early.

name: Arrow of Explosions
entries: When this arrow strikes a solid surface, be it a creature, object, wall, or floor, it explodes with a fiery blast. Each creature within 20 feet of the point of impact must make a DC 17 Dexterity saving throw. A creature takes {@damage 8d6} fire damage on a failed save, or half as much on a successful one. The arrow is destroyed in the blast.

name: Arrow of Glue
entries: An arrow of glue is one of a few arrows known as trick arrows. When you fire an arrow of glue, the arrow's shaft becomes pliant on impact and hardens immediately after. You can fire this arrow at any point you can see within range to cover a 1-foot square area with hardened glue. The GM may rule that especially challenging shots are made with disadvantage. A creature hit by this arrow must succeed a DC 15 Dexterity saving throw or be glued to a nearby surface, unable to move. It can break free with a successful DC 15 Strength ({@skill Athletics}) check.

name: Arrow of Piercing
entries: An arrow of piercing is one of a few arrows known as trick arrows. When you make an attack with this arrow, it becomes a 5-foot-wide line of magical energy that extends out from you to the weapon's normal range. Each creature in that line must make a DC 15 Dexterity saving throw. A creature takes the weapon's normal damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. The arrow is then destroyed.

name: Arrow of Teleportation
entries: An arrow of teleportation is one of a few arrows known as trick arrows. When this arrow is fired from a bow at an unoccupied space within 100 feet of the archer, the archer immediately teleports to its location. The arrow is destroyed on impact.

name: Aura Lenses
entries: A set of these large glass lenses is contained in a single cylindrical case. Each is four inches across, tinted in a different hue, and associated with a particular school of magic, as shown on the following table. When you hold a lens up to your eye and look through it, the world appears to be tinted in the appropriate color, except for creatures and objects which are under the effect of a spell from the lens's associated school of magic, which aren't colored at all.
A complete set of aura lenses contains all 8 individual lenses, but most are found as an incomplete set, containing only {@dice 1d8} of them. In which case this item is of uncommon rarity.

name: Bag of Cheer
entries: This large sack, which weighs 30 pounds and is made from red velvet, appears to be full of presents in colorful wrapping. As an action, you can pull a present from the bag and give it to another creature. The gift is tailored specifically to the recipient; the GM determines its nature or rolls on the table on the following page. The value of the gift can't exceed 100 gp.
Once three presents have been pulled from the bag, the bag can't be used again until the next dawn. Any additional presents removed from the bag are empty but well-decorated boxes.

name: Bedroll of Rest
entries: This enchanted, silken bedroll is immensely comfortable. Sleeping in it during a long rest removes all levels of {@condition exhaustion} and restores all expended Hit Dice. After sleeping in it, you do not require rest for 48 hours, though you can still choose to take a long rest during that time.

name: Bells of Due Alarm
entries: This trio of bells warns you of intruders. You can arrange the bells up to 500 feet apart from each other, and can use your action to speak a command word to cast the {@spell alarm} spell, warding the area between the bells.

name: Blindfold of True Darkness
entries: You have {@sense blindsight} with a range of 10 feet. Within that range, you can effectively see anything that isn't behind {@quickref cover||3||total cover}. Moreover, you can see an {@condition invisible} creature within that range, unless the creature successfully hides from you.

entries.name: Curse
entries: This blindfold is cursed. Attuning to it curses you until you are targeted by the remove curse spell or similar magic. While cursed, you are {@condition blinded}, whether you are wearing the blindfold or not.

name: Bonze's Bokken
entries: This magic weapon deals bludgeoning damage instead of its normal slashing damage. As an action, you can use the bokken to blow a strong wind, dispersing any gases within a 15-foot cube adjacent to you.

When you take the {@action Attack} action while holding this weapon, you can replace one or more of your attacks with concussive waves of sound. Make a ranged spell attack roll with a range of 30/60 feet and a +7 bonus to hit. On a hit, the target takes {@damage 1d10 + 3} thunder damage, and on a critical hit, the target is {@condition deafened}. This attack is audible out to 100 feet.

name: Boots of the Hare
entries: While attuned to these boots, whenever you use your action to {@action Dash}, you gain 90 feet of extra movement instead of the usual amount.

entries.name: Curse
entries: These boots are cursed, a fact that is revealed only when an identify spell is cast on the boots or you attune to them. Attuning to the boots curses you until you are targeted by the remove curse spell or similar magic. While cursed, your speed is 15 feet and can't be increased by any means other than taking the {@action Dash} action.

name: Boots of the Trail
entries: Until they are worn, the boots of the trail appear to be in grave disrepair. When you lace them up, the illusion fades: they are immaculate hiking boots with gold clasps and silk laces. While wearing these boots, you leave behind no tracks or other traces of your passage, and can't be tracked except by magical means. You can march for twice as long before suffering levels of {@condition exhaustion}.

Additionally, you can remove the boots and speak a command word as an action to cause the boots to walk alone, leaving a false trail in any direction for up to one mile. The boots then teleport back to your feet.

name: Bowblade (Melee)
entries: When you use the Switch property of this weapon, it changes to a {@item Bowblade (Ranged)|VSS}.

name: Bowblade (Ranged)
entries: When you use the Switch property of this weapon, it changes to a {@item Bowblade (Melee)|VSS}.

name: Brass Knuckle Revolver (Melee)
entries: When you use the Switch property of this weapon, it changes to a {@item Brass Knuckle Revolver (Ranged)|VSS}.

name: Brass Knuckle Revolver (Ranged)
entries: When you use the Switch property of this weapon, it changes to a {@item Brass Knuckle Revolver (Melee)|VSS}.

name: Brawling Gloves (rare)
reqAttune: by a barbarian, captain, craftsman, fighter, rogue, or warden
entries: While attuned to these fingerless magical gloves, you have proficiency with all improvised weapons and gain a +2 bonus to attack and damage rolls made using them.

name: Brawling Gloves (uncommon)
reqAttune: by a barbarian, captain, craftsman, fighter, rogue, or warden
entries: While attuned to these fingerless magical gloves, you have proficiency with all improvised weapons and gain a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls made using them.

name: Brawling Gloves (very rare)
reqAttune: by a barbarian, captain, craftsman, fighter, rogue, or warden
entries: While attuned to these fingerless magical gloves, you have proficiency with all improvised weapons and gain a +3 bonus to attack and damage rolls made using them.

name: Burning Knuckles
entries: While attuned to these magical gauntlets, your unarmed strikes deal {@damage 2d6} fire damage instead of their usual damage.

name: Cane of Youth
entries: While attuned to this cane, you suffer none of the frailty of old age and can't be aged magically. You can still die of old age, however.

name: Chameleon Concoction
entries: When you drink this potion, your skin camouflages to match the color and texture of your surroundings, granting you advantage on Dexterity ({@skill Stealth}) checks you make to avoid being seen for 1 hour. This liquid's hue rapidly shifts to match whatever material it is nearest to.

name: Coil of Strength Storing
entries: This metallic coil is usually worn on an arm or leg. While attuned to it, whenever you make a melee weapon attack against a hostile creature that exceeds the target's AC by 5 or more, the coil gains 1 stored charge. It can hold up to 5 charges at a time.

When you make an attack with a melee weapon, you can expend any number of stored charges to gain a bonus on the attack roll equal to the number of charges expended. You can wait until after you roll the {@dice d20} before deciding to expend charges, but must decide before the GM says whether the attack hits or misses. Unused charges disappear 1 minute after being stored.

name: Crossbow, Axe (Melee)
entries: When you use the Switch property of this weapon, it changes to a {@item Crossbow, Axe (Ranged)|VSS}.

name: Crossbow, Axe (Ranged)
entries: When you use the Switch property of this weapon, it changes to a {@item Crossbow, Axe (Melee)|VSS}.

name: Cure-All
entries: The cure-all contains {@dice 1d4 + 1} doses of potent medicine. As an action, you can drink a dose, curing you of any disease, ending your poisoning, and causing you to be immune to being {@condition poisoned} for 1 hour. A complex swirl of red liquid in the potion's center resembles a snake on a pole. Shaking the bottle fails to mix the potion's contents.

name: Deckhammer (Blade)
entries: When you use the Switch property of this weapon, it changes to a {@item Deckhammer (Blunt)|VSS}.

name: Deckhammer (Blunt)
entries: When you use the Switch property of this weapon, it changes to a {@item Deckhammer (Blade)|VSS}.

name: Dowsing Rod
entries: This forked stick is used to discover water. It has 3 charges and regains {@dice 1d3} expended charges daily at dawn. While holding this rod, you can use your action and expend a charge to cause the rod to point to the largest source of water in a 10-mile radius. The rod doesn't indicate the distance or quantity of water. If there is little to no water to be found, the rod indicates vaguely downward, for there is always some amount of water underground.

name: Drum of Blasted Beats
entries: This {@item drum|PHB} has 6 charges. While attuned to it, you can use an action to strike it and expend one charge to cast the {@spell thunderwave} spell, or two charges to cast the {@spell shatter} spell (save DC 15).

The {@item drum|PHB} regains {@dice 1d6} expended charges daily at dusk. If you expend the {@item drum|PHB|drum's} last charge, roll a {@dice d20}. On a 1, the {@item drum|PHB} ruptures and loses its magic.

name: Flutterby Rod
entries: This rod has 7 charges and regains {@dice 1d6 + 1} expended charges daily at dawn. While holding the rod, you can use it to cast the {@spell light} cantrip on itself at will.

As an action, you can expend a charge to shoot a shimmering, green, butterfly-shaped flutterbolt at a target within 60 feet. Make a ranged spell attack with a +5 attack bonus. On a hit, the target takes {@damage 1d4 + 1} force damage and is outlined in sparkling green butterflies. The next attack roll made against this target before the end of your next turn has advantage, and the target can't benefit from being {@condition invisible} until the end of your next turn.

name: Folding Ladder
entries: This item appears as two short wooden rods, 12 inches long and 1 inch in diameter, connected side by side. It weighs four pounds. It has three command words.

When you speak the ladder's first command word, it expands into a ladder, 2 feet wide and 20 feet long. If you speak the second command word, it extends into a freestanding stepladder, 30 feet high with a base that is 5 feet by 10 feet. The third command word causes the ladder to collapse back into its folded form.
The ladder can support 500 pounds of weight in either of its extended configurations.

name: Gambler's Coin
entries: This ordinary looking gold piece has deep scratches on one side. It has 3 charges. When you make an ability check, attack roll, or saving throw while holding it, you can expend 1 charge to replace the {@dice d20} roll with a {@coinflip coinflip|Gambler's Coin|Heads (20)|Tails (1)}. On heads, the roll is treated as a 20 (though you do not score a critical hit with an attack roll or activate any other effects which trigger on the roll of a 20), and on tails, the roll is treated as a 1. The coin regains all expended charges at dawn.

name: Gaol Net
entries: When a Large or smaller creature is {@condition restrained} with this magical net, you can use your bonus action to speak its command word, causing the net to transform into a Large iron cage that encloses the target. The enclosed creature is no longer {@condition restrained}.

The cage weighs 500 pounds and is fitted with a locked door (DC 15 to pick the lock). A creature, including the one enclosed in the cage, can use an action to make a DC 25 Strength check to bend the bars enough to let a creature out. If the cage is empty, you can use an action to speak a command word, causing it to transform back into a net.
Once the net transforms into a cage, it can't do so again until the next dawn.

name: Gauntlet of the Grandmaster (rare)
entries: While wearing this gauntlet, you can use it as a spellcasting focus for your warmage spells, and you gain a +2 bonus to spell attack and damage rolls and to the saving throw DCs of your warmage spells. This gauntlet counts as a specially prepared gauntlet for cantrips such as force buckler.

In addition, you gain one of the following cantrips of your choice: {@spell force buckler|VSS}, {@spell force dart|VSS}, or {@spell force weapon|VSS}. The cantrip doesn't count against your number of cantrips known. Whenever you finish a long rest, you can change your selection.

name: Gauntlet of the Grandmaster (uncommon)
entries: While wearing this gauntlet, you can use it as a spellcasting focus for your warmage spells, and you gain a +1 bonus to spell attack and damage rolls and to the saving throw DCs of your warmage spells. This gauntlet counts as a specially prepared gauntlet for cantrips such as force buckler.

In addition, you gain one of the following cantrips of your choice: {@spell force buckler|VSS}, {@spell force dart|VSS}, or {@spell force weapon|VSS}. The cantrip doesn't count against your number of cantrips known. Whenever you finish a long rest, you can change your selection.

name: Gauntlet of the Grandmaster (very rare)
entries: While wearing this gauntlet, you can use it as a spellcasting focus for your warmage spells, and you gain a +3 bonus to spell attack and damage rolls and to the saving throw DCs of your warmage spells. This gauntlet counts as a specially prepared gauntlet for cantrips such as force buckler.

In addition, you gain one of the following cantrips of your choice: {@spell force buckler|VSS}, {@spell force dart|VSS}, or {@spell force weapon|VSS}. The cantrip doesn't count against your number of cantrips known. Whenever you finish a long rest, you can change your selection.

name: Glimmerbolt (Hand)
entries: You have a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon.

This weapon has 10 charges and regains {@dice 1d6 + 4} charges daily at dawn. As part of your {@action Attack} action, you can expend a charge to create and load a piece of radiant ammunition into the crossbow. This bolt deals an extra {@damage 1d6} damage on a hit and deals radiant damage, instead of its normal piercing damage.

Additionally, as an action, you can expend 3 charges to load a blinding bolt of light into the crossbow and fire it at a point you can see within 60 feet, where it detonates in a flash. Each creature within 20 feet of that point must succeed on a DC 17 Constitution saving throw or be {@condition blinded} until the end of your next turn. Motes of light hang in the air around that point for the next minute, shedding bright light in a 20-foot radius and dim light for an additional 20 feet.

name: Glimmerbolt (Heavy)
entries: You have a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon.

This weapon has 10 charges and regains {@dice 1d6 + 4} charges daily at dawn. As part of your {@action Attack} action, you can expend a charge to create and load a piece of radiant ammunition into the crossbow. This bolt deals an extra {@damage 1d6} damage on a hit and deals radiant damage, instead of its normal piercing damage.

Additionally, as an action, you can expend 3 charges to load a blinding bolt of light into the crossbow and fire it at a point you can see within 60 feet, where it detonates in a flash. Each creature within 20 feet of that point must succeed on a DC 17 Constitution saving throw or be {@condition blinded} until the end of your next turn. Motes of light hang in the air around that point for the next minute, shedding bright light in a 20-foot radius and dim light for an additional 20 feet.

name: Gloves of Skill
entries: While attuned to these gloves, you have proficiency with one tool or instrument. The DM chooses the proficiency or determines it randomly from the options below.

name: Graverobber's Spade (Rare)
entries: You can use this magic weapon as a spellcasting focus for your necromancer spells. While holding this magic weapon, you gain a +2 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with it, and you gain a bonus to spell attack rolls and the saving throw DCs of your necromancer spells. The bonus is determined by the weapon's rarity.
Additionally, you can cast the {@spell exhume|VSS} spell at will without using a spell slot or material components.

name: Graverobber's Spade (Uncommon)
entries: You can use this magic weapon as a spellcasting focus for your necromancer spells. While holding this magic weapon, you gain a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with it, and you gain a bonus to spell attack rolls and the saving throw DCs of your necromancer spells. The bonus is determined by the weapon's rarity.
Additionally, you can cast the {@spell exhume|VSS} spell at will without using a spell slot or material components.

name: Graverobber's Spade (Very rare)
entries: You can use this magic weapon as a spellcasting focus for your necromancer spells. While holding this magic weapon, you gain a +3 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with it, and you gain a bonus to spell attack rolls and the saving throw DCs of your necromancer spells. The bonus is determined by the weapon's rarity.
Additionally, you can cast the {@spell exhume|VSS} spell at will without using a spell slot or material components.

name: Gunsword (Melee)
entries: When you use the Switch property of this weapon, it changes to a {@item Gunsword (Ranged)|VSS}.

name: Gunsword (Ranged)
entries: When you use the Switch property of this weapon, it changes to a {@item Gunsword (Melee)|VSS}.

name: Hand of Glory
entries: This mummified hand is worn around the neck with a leather cord. While attuned to the hand, you gain two additional attunement slots for magic rings, which are placed on the hand's digits. If your attunement with the hand ends, your attunement with the magic rings worn on it also ends.

name: Hinge Spear (Double)
entries: When you use the Switch property of this weapon, it changes to a {@item Hinge Spear (Single)|VSS}.

name: Hinge Spear (Single)
entries: When you use the Switch property of this weapon, it changes to a {@item Hinge Spear (Double)|VSS}.

name: Invisible Ink
entries: Anything written in this ink is {@condition invisible}. A DC 25 Intelligence ({@skill Investigation}) check reveals that there is writing present, but not what it says. Only creatures that have {@sense truesight} or are under the effect of the see invisibility spell can read text written in this ink, though the invisibility effect can be removed using {@spell dispel magic}. One pot is sufficient to write 250 words or draw one picture or diagram.

name: Jax
entries: Rather than drinking this vial of orange, brackish liquid, you inject into your body as an action. Once injected, for 1 hour, your Strength, Dexterity, and Constitution scores each increase by 4, and the maximum for these scores is increased to 24. However, your maximum hit points are permanently reduced by {@dice 1d12}. No means short of a greater restoration or wish spell can restore hit points lost in this way.

You can use more than one dose of jax at once, and its ability score increases stack for the 1-hour duration. However, you still suffer the reduction to your maximum hit points each time you take an additional dose, and you must succeed a DC 20 Constitution saving throw or suffer an overdose. When you overdose, you are reduced to 0 hit points and can't regain hit points for 1 hour.

name: Kusarigama (Chain)
entries: When you use the Switch property of this weapon, it changes to a {@item Kusarigama (Handle)|VSS}.

name: Kusarigama (Handle)
entries: When you use the Switch property of this weapon, it changes to a {@item Kusarigama (Chain)|VSS}.

name: Lady and Lord Rings
entries: These two rings, one engraved with the image of a mighty lord and the other with a stately lady, are part of a matched set. Two creatures can attune to the rings, each wearing one of the rings. While within 30 feet of each other, both attuned creatures have resistance to all damage. Additionally, while both creatures are within 30 feet of each other, each time an attuned creature takes damage, the other creature loses the same number of hit points. Attunement to these rings breaks if either attuned creature drops to 0 hit points or breaks attunement.

name: Leaden Manacles
entries: These manacles behave the same as normal manacles with the following addition: a creature that attempts to cast a spell while wearing the manacles must make a DC 12 ability check using its spellcasting ability. On a failure, the spell fails and has no effect; the spell slot is expended, the action is wasted, and the manacled creature takes {@damage 1d6} fire damage per level of the spell slot expended. On a success, the creature takes half as much damage and the spell is cast successfully.

name: Locket of Remembrance
entries: When a locket of remembrance is created, it is engraved with the name and likeness of a creature that has died. It is then dedicated to this creature. As long as the locket is worn by a living creature, the remembered creature's remains can't become undead, and its soul can't linger as an undead creature.

name: Loincloth of Oni Magic
entries: While attuned to this blood-red loincloth, you can cast and concentrate on any spells you know, even while you are raging.

Furthermore, the loincloth has 6 charges. While attuned to it, you can use an action to expend 1 or more charges to cast one of the following spells (save DC 17): {@spell charm person} (1 charge), {@spell sleep} (1 charge), {@spell darkness} (2 charges), {@spell invisibility} (2 charges), {@spell gaseous form} (3 charges), or {@spell cone of cold} (4 charges). The loincloth regains {@dice 1d6} expended charges daily at dusk.

name: Marvelous Painted World
entries: This masterful painting, at least a 5-foot square in area, was crafted by a master painter using at least ten pots of marvelous pigments. It depicts a serene painted world. The painting itself acts as a portal to a demiplane in which the painted world exists, and is large enough to allow Medium creatures to pass through unhindered. Inside the painted world, a misty archway is a portal to the real world. If the painting is rolled up or faced toward a solid surface, the portal disappears inside the painted world.

The location, objects, and creatures depicted within the painted world are determined by the painting's creator, but such objects and creatures can't leave the painted world, as they can't pass through the portal, and disappear into smoke if removed from the demiplane by other means. Time passes at half speed within the painted world, and you don't need to eat or drink while within it.

name: Morbid Makeup
entries: This makeup kit contains only red, white, and black paint. It functions as a {@item disguise kit|PHB} which lets you convincingly appear as a fey, fiend, or undead creature. While wearing the makeup, you have advantage on Charisma ({@skill Intimidation}) checks you make against humanoids.
The kit contains enough makeup for 10 applications. Each application lasts up to 8 hours, and can be washed off as an action.

name: Mouse of Cowardice
entries: This wind-up clockwork mouse terrifies even the largest beasts. When you speak its command word and set it rolling toward a Large or larger creature within 15 feet of you as an action, you cast the spell {@spell phantasmal killer} (save DC 15) using the mouse. The mouse can't be used this way again until the next dawn.

name: Necromantic Draught
entries: Pouring this potion on a Medium or Small humanoid corpse causes the effect of the animate dead spell for 24 hours. You command undead animated in this way. This brightly glowing neonyellow goo is repelled away from living things which touch its container.

name: Ooze Bottle
entries: As an action, you can throw this vial up to 20 feet, shattering it on impact and releasing a gray ooze.
This ooze is friendly to you and your allies, and will otherwise attack the nearest creature it can detect.

If there is no creature to attack, the ooze will follow you. However, the biochemistry of this ooze is unstable, and the ooze dissolves into a lifeless sludge after 1 hour. The charcoal-colored liquid inside this bottle seems to lunge about with unnatural momentum.

name: Parchment of Sending
entries: This parchment can hold a message of twenty-five words or less; additional text is magically erased. When addressed with the name of a creature with which you are familiar, the parchment folds itself into the shape of a glider and flutters on the wind, magically seeking out the creature within 24 hours if the recipient is on the same plane of existence as you. The recipient can write an additional twenty-five word message, and cause the parchment to fold itself and return to you by addressing it to your name. The parchment can make four such trips, and then becomes mundane parchment.

name: Pentacle of Woe (rare)
entries: While attuned to this medallion, you gain a +1 bonus to spell attack rolls and to the saving throw DCs of your witch hexes and spells. This bonus is determined by the pentacle's rarity.
In addition, this pentacle has 3 charges. You can expend a charge to cast a hex that usually takes an action as a bonus action instead. The pentacle regains all expended charges daily at dusk.

name: Pentacle of Woe (uncommon)
entries: While attuned to this medallion, you gain a +1 bonus to spell attack rolls and to the saving throw DCs of your witch hexes and spells. This bonus is determined by the pentacle's rarity.
In addition, this pentacle has 3 charges. You can expend a charge to cast a hex that usually takes an action as a bonus action instead. The pentacle regains all expended charges daily at dusk.

name: Pentacle of Woe (very rare)
entries: While attuned to this medallion, you gain a +1 bonus to spell attack rolls and to the saving throw DCs of your witch hexes and spells. This bonus is determined by the pentacle's rarity.
In addition, this pentacle has 3 charges. You can expend a charge to cast a hex that usually takes an action as a bonus action instead. The pentacle regains all expended charges daily at dusk.

name: Phase Arrow
entries: This ethereal arrow passes through all matter except the intended target. You ignore all cover, including full cover, when making an attack with this arrow.
This arrow can target creatures on the Ethereal Plane as if they were on the Material Plane, and vice versa.
Once it hits a target, the arrow is no longer magical.

name: Polymorph Potion
entries: When you drink this potion, which is a purple liquid derived from mimic blood, you gain the effects of the polymorph spell for an hour. Roll a {@dice d20} and consult the following table to determine the form you are transformed into.

name: Portal Chalk
entries: Each of these two pieces of chalk radiate a different luminescent aura: one orange, the other blue. Each piece of chalk has 10 uses. As an action, you can expend one use of a piece of chalk to draw a circular or rectangular portal on a solid stone surface large enough for a Medium creature. This portal instantly becomes linked to the most recent portal drawn with the other color of chalk, unlinking any portals created by these pieces of chalk other than these two. A linked portal is a glowing ring or rectangle filled with opaque mist; an unlinked portal is simply mundane chalk. A pair of linked portals acts as a magical gate. Any creature or object entering a linked portal exits from the other portal as if the two were adjacent to each other.

name: Potion of Mirrored Eyes
entries: For 1 minute after you drink this potion, you gain immunity to any effect which can normally be avoided by averting your gaze from it, such as a medusa's petrifying gaze. While under the influence of this potion, you can safely look at such creatures without being subjected to their abilities.

name: Puzzle Box
entries: Though a magic item in and of itself, this cubic box often contains far more powerful and destructive items. The puzzle box can hold one cubic foot of contents, which can't be targeted by divination spells or perceived through scrying sensors created by divination spells.

Once the box is closed, it can only be opened by solving the box's puzzle. You can attempt to solve it by spending 24 hours working on the puzzle mechanism, after which you must succeed a DC 23 Intelligence check to open the box. You can close the box as an action, automatically scrambling the puzzle.

name: Reaper's Bullet
entries: This bullet, forged by the reaper and engraved with insidious runes, brings inevitable death on its target.
A creature hit by this bullet dies.

name: Replacement Man
entries: If damage would reduce you to 0 hit points while you are attuned to this humanoid figurine, you drop to 1 hit point instead and the figurine fades away with a sad smile on his face.

name: Replica Clay
entries: When you touch this lump of clay to an object that can fit within a 5-foot cube, the clay shifts and molds into an exact replica with the same color and texture. The replica even mimics visual magical elements, such as glowing runes. Touching the replica reveals it to be made of clay, as it yields under any significant force, but it is impossible to distinguish with a visual inspection. Once the clay is shaped into a replica, it becomes nonmagical.

name: Reverberating Shield
entries: While holding this shield, you have a +1 bonus to AC. This bonus is in addition to the shield's normal bonus to AC. Whenever a creature misses you with a melee weapon attack while you are holding this shield, it must succeed a DC 15 Dexterity saving throw. On a failure, the creature drops its weapon, which is thrown 15 feet away from you. If the weapon can't be dropped, such as a dragon's bite or claws, the attacker instead has disadvantage on all weapon attacks until the end of its turn.

name: Rifle Spear (Melee)
entries: When you use the Switch property of this weapon, it changes to a {@item Rifle Spear (Ranged)|VSS}.

name: Rifle Spear (Ranged)
entries: When you use the Switch property of this weapon, it changes to a {@item Rifle Spear (Melee)|VSS}.

name: Ring of Icebergs
entries: As a bonus action, or a reaction to being hit by an attacker you can see, you can spin the ring's jewel, causing it to expand into a hollow block of clear ice that completely surrounds you. This iceberg occupies your space and pushes creatures within your space to the nearest unoccupied area, ending any {@action grapple} in which you are involved. There is enough room within the iceberg to move around, but you can't move more than 6 inches in any direction. Spells and other magical effects can't extend through the iceberg or be cast through it.

The iceberg is an object with AC 10 and 100 HP. If it was activated as a reaction, it takes as much of the triggering damage as possible. The iceberg has immunity to cold, poison, and psychic damage, and vulnerability to fire damage. The icy tomb lasts for up to 1 minute, until it is destroyed, or until you use a bonus action to cease the jewel's spinning.
Once you spin the ring to create an iceberg, you can't do so again until the following dawn.

name: Ring of Salvation
entries: If you fail a saving throw while attuned to this ring, you can choose to succeed it instead. Once you use this ability, you can't do so again until the next dawn.

name: Sandstone Solution
entries: You can pour this substance on the ground as an action. If poured onto stone, a 10-foot deep, 10-foot radius portion of the stone becomes mud for 1 hour.

When poured into mud, sand, or quicksand, a 10-foot deep, 10-foot-radius region of the material become solid stone for 1 hour. The stone has AC 17, 75 HP, and immunity to psychic and poison damage. Any creature inside it when it becomes stone must make a DC 14 Dexterity saving throw or be {@condition restrained}. The {@condition restrained} creature can break free by succeeding on a DC 20 Strength check or by dealing 25 damage to the stone. This sandlike substance flows about its container like a fluid.

name: Scroll of Duplication
entries: This blank scroll is imbued with enchantments that enable it to copy text from another source. As an action, you can touch the scroll of duplication to an object that contains writing. The scroll instantaneously copies up to 500 consecutive words from the source material (you can choose which section if the source material is longer than this), creating a perfect duplicate of the original text. The scroll only copies nonmagical text, not illustrations or magical writings (such as the contents of a spellbook or a glyph of warding). If the source contains a mixture of magical writing, illustrations, and nonmagical text, only the nonmagical text is copied, leaving blank space where illustrations and magical writing would be expected. Using the scroll doesn't activate magical traps that trigger upon reading the source material.

name: Shotgun Axe (Melee)
entries: When you use the Switch property of this weapon, it changes to a {@item Shotgun Axe (Ranged)|VSS}.

name: Shotgun Axe (Ranged)
entries: When you use the Switch property of this weapon, it changes to a {@item Shotgun Axe (Melee)|VSS}.

name: Skitterlegs
entries: Worn like a backpack, these brass and mithral legs deploy when you're knocked out or {@condition paralyzed}. A series of switches allows you to program the legs with either the "Defend" or "Eliminate" setting, as well as a list of friendly creatures in order of priority.

Whenever you are {@condition paralyzed} or knocked {@condition unconscious} (except when {@condition unconscious} due to nonmagical sleep), the skitterlegs deploy, lifting your body from the ground. While the legs are deployed, you don't count as being {@condition prone}. Attacks made against you while the legs are deployed aren't critical hits, even though you are {@condition paralyzed} or {@condition unconscious}. The legs make Strength and Dexterity checks and saving throws with a +5 modifier. The legs have a walking speed of 30 feet. On each of your turns while you are {@condition paralyzed} or {@condition unconscious}, the legs behave according to their settings:

entries.name: Defend
entries: The legs take the {@action Dodge} or {@action Disengage} action (your choice when you program the legs) and move toward the highest-priority friendly creature who is still conscious.

entries.name: Eliminate
entries: The legs move toward the nearest hostile creature and make two melee attacks with an attack bonus of +7. On a hit, the legs deal {@damage 1d8 + 2} piercing damage.

If you regain consciousness or recover from paralysis, the legs set you back on your feet before retracting. The legs can function for one cumulative hour each day. If this duration is exceeded, the legs collapse and drop you {@condition prone}.

name: Smoking pipe of Dragon's Breath
entries: This pipe has 2 charges and regains 1 expended charge daily at dawn. If the pipe is full of one ounce of smoking herb, you can use an action and expend 1 charge to inhale deeply from it and exhale dragon's flame. Each creature in a 30-foot-radius cone must make a DC 15 Dexterity saving throw or take {@damage 8d6} fire damage, or half as much on a successful one.

name: Sorting Beast
entries: The sorting beast is a six-legged construct with eyes, legs, and antennae at both ends, as well as an array of measuring devices near its center. It can manipulate and hold objects up to 30 pounds in weight.

When activated as an action, the sorting beast sets about collecting and sorting all loose valuable items within 100 feet. It sorts all gold pieces, silver pieces, and copper pieces into neat stacks of 10. For material goods, such as precious stones, the sorting beast can appraise value by weight and quality, before sorting the goods appropriately and printing the results on a fine paper strip. The sorting beast continues sorting until finished or deactivated as an action.
Additionally, the sorting beast can cast the spell {@spell identify}, without using material components, on one object you designate each day.

name: Split Staff (Combined)
entries: When you use the Switch property of this weapon, it changes into 2 {@item Split Staff (Split)|VSS}.

name: Split Staff (Split)
entries: When you use the Switch property of 2 of these weapons, they change into a {@item Split Staff (Combined)|VSS}.

name: Split Swords (Combined)
entries: When you use the Switch property of this weapon, it changes into 2 {@item Split Swords (Split)|VSS}.

name: Split Swords (Split)
entries: When you use the Switch property of 2 of these weapons, they change into a {@item Split Swords (Combined)|VSS}.

name: Switch Amalgam
entries: This mixture of mithral, quicksilver, and platinum molds easily and adheres to steel, allowing a trained craftsman to make unique compound weapons.

While attuned to the amalgam, you can spend a minute heating the amalgam and carefully attaching it to a weapon or removing it from one. The amalgam can be attached to two weapons at a time. Once attached to two weapons, the weapons become magical, and each gains a +1 bonus to its attack and damage rolls, unless it is a magic weapon that already has a bonus to those rolls.

Additionally, each weapon gains the Switch property. A switch weapon has two forms; you can swap between which weapon is being used at any time, even between attacks. Unlike other switch weapons, weapons unified with the amalgam do not become exotic weapons.

name: Tome of Tongues
entries: This book contains grammar and vocabulary for a specific language, and its words are charged with magic. If you spend 8 hours over a period of 2 days or fewer studying the book's contents and practicing its guidelines, you learn to read, write, and speak whatever language it concerns. The tome then loses its magic forever.

name: Totem of Enmity
entries: This wooden rod is engraved with evil symbols and hateful curses in all languages. As an action, you can break the rod while speaking the name of a creature you are familiar with to swear vengeance against that creature. You indefinitely have advantage on attack rolls against the named creature. This effect ends if you break another totem of enmity or the creature dies.

name: Troll Rod
entries: This uncouth pommel has a troll's arm attached—still living—to one end. As a bonus action, you can issue it commands in the troll dialect of Giant to pick up items, drop them, or make a fist (typical command words include "grabbit," "leggo," and "maik'a'fist.") If closed into a fist, the rod acts as a magic mace, and you have a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls made using it.

name: Universal Knocker
entries: You can use your action to hold this brass door knocker against an object to cast the {@spell knock} spell targeting the object. The knocker can't be used this way again until the next dawn.

name: Weapon Charms
entries: A weapon charm is a small ornament fixed on a loop of string or chain. You can use your action to attach the charm on a weapon, usually on the weapon's pommel, causing the weapon to become a magic weapon that requires attunement. Even if the weapon was already magical, you must attune to it again to gain the charm's magical benefits, which are listed in the charm's description. A weapon can only have one charm attached at a time.

entries.name: Bat (Uncommon)
entries: This obsidian charm appears like a shrieking bat. While attached, when you deal damage to a creature with this weapon, its hit point maximum is reduced by an amount equal to the damage taken. This reduction lasts until the creature finishes a long rest. The creature dies if this effect reduces its hit point maximum to 0.

entries.name: Blade (Uncommon)
entries: This adamantine charm is shaped like a miniature longsword. While attached, you have a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon. This bonus doesn't apply to magical weapons that already have a bonus to attack and damage rolls.

entries.name: Die (Uncommon)
entries: This silver charm depicts a six-sided die. While attached, the weapon deals more potent critical hits. When you score a critical hit, if you roll the maximum number on any damage die, you can roll an extra damage die and add its damage to the total, rolling again if this die is also the maximum number, and so on. You can roll a total number of damage dice for this critical hit equal to twice the number of damage dice you initially rolled.

entries.name: Feather (Common)
entries: This gold charm of a feather feels unusually light. While attached, this weapon weighs half as much as usual. Small creatures can effectively use the weapon, even if it has the Heavy property.

entries.name: Ghost (Common)
entries: This crystal charm is carved into the shape of a wispy spirit. While attached, the weapon can affect creatures on the Ethereal Plane as if they were on the Material Plane, and vice versa.

entries.name: Hook (Common)
entries: This bronze charm is shaped like a fishing hook. When attached, if the weapon is on the same plane of existence, you can use your bonus action to teleport it to your hand.

entries.name: Lance (Uncommon)
entries: This copper charm depicts a short lance. While attached, once on each of your turns when you make a melee attack with this weapon against a creature you can see, you can lunge up to 15 feet toward your target before making the attack. This movement doesn't provoke opportunity attacks. You can perform this movement even if it causes you to travel through the air, though you fall after making the attack if you do not land on solid ground.

entries.name: Lightning Bolt (Uncommon)
entries: This mithral charm depicts a wild lightning bolt. While attached, this weapon deals an extra {@damage 1d6} lightning damage to any target it hits.

entries.name: Mirror (Rare)
entries: This shiny platinum charm depicts an elegant hand mirror. This charm can only be attached to a weapon with the Light property. When attached, when you draw the weapon with one hand, a spectral duplicate of the weapon appears in your other hand. This spectral duplicate has identical statistics to the original weapon, including its magical effects, but doesn't include ammunition. When the attached weapon or its spectral duplicate leaves your hand, the duplicate vanishes.

name: Whip Sword (Sword)
entries: When you use the Switch property of this weapon, it changes to a {@item Whip Sword (Whip)|VSS}.

name: Whip Sword (Whip)
entries: When you use the Switch property of this weapon, it changes to a {@item Whip Sword (Sword)|VSS}.

name: Wooden Coin of Lies
entries: While attuned to this coin, you are constantly under the effect of the {@spell glibness} spell.

entries.name: Curse
entries: This coin is cursed; attuning to it extends its curse to you. You can only break attunement to the coin with the {@spell remove curse} spell or similar magic. While attuned to the coin, you can't deliberately speak the truth. You can be evasive in your wording, lie by omission, or speak half-truths, as long as your words remain within the boundaries of deception.

name: Émigré Manuscript
entries: This ancient tome is shaped like a skull and smells either of violets or tiger lilies. While holding the tome, you can cast the spell {@spell resurrection} without using material components. Once the manuscript is used, it can't be used again until the next dawn.

entries.name: Curse
entries: The émigré manuscript is cursed to bring nothing but misery to those who use it. Whenever you use it to raise the dead, roll a {@dice d20} to determine the result according to the following table.

rows: The spell fails and the caster immediately dies.
The target is resurrected as a revenant, seeking revenge against the caster.
The target is resurrected as a ghost, but otherwise retains their memories and personality.
The spell works, but the 100 humanoids nearest to the target (excluding the caster) immediately die.
The spell works, but the caster must roll twice on the Indefinite Madness table, suffering both results. If the same result is rolled twice, the caster immediately dies.
The spell works, but the target loses all of their memories, class levels, proficiencies (including languages), and personality traits.
The spell appears to work, but the target dies again after {@dice 1d10} minutes. No magic short of a {@spell wish} can revive them from this death.

name: Amphibious Adaptation
entries: {@i Donor: Any Creature with the Amphibious or Water Breathing Trait}
This graft attaches the fins and gills of an aquatic creature to your body. You have a {@variantrule Swim Speed|XPHB} equal to your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} and you can breathe air and water.

name: Angelic Wings
entries: {@i Donor: Any Celestial with a {@variantrule Fly Speed|XPHB}}
While this graft is attached, you have a {@variantrule Fly Speed|XPHB} equal to your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB}.

name: Antimagic Eye
entries: {@i Donor: Any Creature with Magic Resistance Trait}

You can use this graft to cast {@spell Dispel Magic|XPHB}. Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma is your spellcasting ability for this spell when you cast it with this graft (choose each time you install this graft). When you cast the spell using this graft, the level of spell that you automatically end on the target is determined by the donor's {@variantrule Challenge Rating|XPHB}, as shown on the Antimagic Eyes table.
Once you activate this graft, you can't do so again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

name: Arcane Synapses
entries: {@i Donor: Any Creature with the Spellcasting Action}

These additional nerves grant arcane potential once installed in the brain. The GM chooses one of the donor's spells. You always have that spell prepared. You can cast it once using this graft without expending a spell slot. Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma is your spellcasting ability for this spell when you cast it with this graft (choose each time you install this graft).

name: Aura Lenses (Complete)
entries: A set of these large glass lenses is contained in a single cylindrical case. Each is four inches across, tinted in a different hue, and associated with a particular school of magic, as shown on the following table. When you hold a lens up to your eye and look through it as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, the world appears to be tinted in the lens's color, except for creatures and objects that are under the effect of a spell from the lens's associated school of magic, which appear normally colored. A complete set of Aura Lenses contains 8 lenses, each associated with a school of magic, but most are found as an incomplete set, containing only {@dice 1d8} of them.

name: Aura Lenses (Incomplete)
entries: A set of these large glass lenses is contained in a single cylindrical case. Each is four inches across, tinted in a different hue, and associated with a particular school of magic, as shown on the following table. When you hold a lens up to your eye and look through it as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, the world appears to be tinted in the lens's color, except for creatures and objects that are under the effect of a spell from the lens's associated school of magic, which appear normally colored. A complete set of Aura Lenses contains 8 lenses, each associated with a school of magic, but most are found as an incomplete set, containing only {@dice 1d8} of them.

name: Ball Bearings
entries: As a {@action Utilize|XPHB} action, you spill Ball Bearings from their pouch. They spread to cover a level, 10-foot-square area within 10 feet of yourself. A creature that enters this area for the first time on a turn must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw or have the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition. It takes 10 minutes to recover the Ball Bearings.

name: Ballista Trap
entries: As a {@action Utilize|XPHB} action, you load this compact, Ballista Trap in an unoccupied space within 5 feet of you and aim it in a direction you choose. The trap triggers when a creature enters the area within a 30-foot-long, 5-foot-wide {@variantrule Line [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Line} extending from the trap for the first time on a turn or ends its turn there. The Ballista Trap makes a ranged attack roll (bonus equals your Intelligence modifier plus your Masterwork Bonus and {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}). On a hit, the target takes Piercing damage equal to {@dice 1d8}. A creature can only trigger one Ballista Trap per turn. It takes a {@action Utilize|XPHB} action to recover the Ballista Trap.

name: Bottled Ooze (Black Pudding)
entries: As {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can throw this bottle up to 60 feet, shattering it on impact and releasing a {@creature Black Pudding|XMM}. This ooze is friendly to you and your allies, and will otherwise attack the nearest creature it can detect. If there is no creature to attack, the ooze will follow you. The ooze dissolves into a lifeless sludge after 1 hour or when you release another Bottled Ooze.

name: Bottled Ooze (Gelatinous Cube)
entries: As {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can throw this bottle up to 60 feet, shattering it on impact and releasing a {@creature Gelatinous Cube|XMM}. This ooze is friendly to you and your allies, and will otherwise attack the nearest creature it can detect. If there is no creature to attack, the ooze will follow you. The ooze dissolves into a lifeless sludge after 1 hour or when you release another Bottled Ooze.

name: Bottled Ooze (Gray Ooze)
entries: As {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can throw this bottle up to 60 feet, shattering it on impact and releasing a {@creature Gray Ooze|XMM}. This ooze is friendly to you and your allies, and will otherwise attack the nearest creature it can detect. If there is no creature to attack, the ooze will follow you. The ooze dissolves into a lifeless sludge after 1 hour or when you release another Bottled Ooze.

name: Bottled Ooze (Ochre Jelly)
entries: As {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can throw this bottle up to 60 feet, shattering it on impact and releasing a {@creature Ochre Jelly|XMM}. This ooze is friendly to you and your allies, and will otherwise attack the nearest creature it can detect. If there is no creature to attack, the ooze will follow you. The ooze dissolves into a lifeless sludge after 1 hour or when you release another Bottled Ooze.

name: Burrowing Adaptation
entries: {@i Donor: Any Creature with a {@variantrule Burrow Speed|XPHB} of 10+ Feet}
You have a {@variantrule Burrow Speed|XPHB} equal to half your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB}. You can dig through sand, earth, mud, or ice, but you can't burrow through solid rock.

name: Caltrops
entries: As a {@action Utilize|XPHB} action, you spread Caltrops from their bag to cover a 5-foot-square area within 5 feet of yourself. A creature that enters this area for the first time on a turn must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw or take 1 Piercing damage and have its {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} reduced to 0 until the start of its next turn. It takes 10 minutes to recover the Caltrops.

name: Climbing Apparatus
entries: {@i Donor: Any Creature with a {@variantrule Climb Speed|XPHB}}
Once attached, this graft allows you to cling to surfaces and climb with agility. You gain a {@variantrule Climb Speed|XPHB} equal to your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB}.

name: Crimson Compass
entries: As a {@action Magic|XPHB} action, you can insert a drop of blood into the face of this compass, which orients itself as a needle. The needle points to the creature to whom the blood belongs if it is alive and on the same plane of existence. Otherwise, the needle swings wildly. The compass can't locate a creature under the effects of the {@spell Nondetection|XPHB} spell. You can remove the blood from the compass as a {@action Magic|XPHB} action.

name: Dire Diary
entries: This diary contains 50 yellowed pages. When you attune to it, you find that the pages contain your own handwriting about events yet to come. No other creature can thereafter attune to the diary. You can use the journal to cast Dire Warning from it, filling one page of the diary with a message from the future of up to 50 words. The message may consist of a sketch or diagram, instead of writing, and is usually vague or cryptic in order to avoid paradoxes. The diary can't cast this spell again for 7 days.

name: Draconis Fundamentum
entries: {@i Donor: Any Dragon with a Breath Weapon, Such as Fire Breath}

This graft installs the source of breath weapons into your body. When you take the {@action Attack|XPHB} action on your turn, you can replace one of your attacks with an exhalation of magical energy in a {@variantrule Cone [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Cone}. Each creature in that {@variantrule Cone [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Cone} must make a Dexterity saving throw, taking damage as shown on the Draconis Fundamentum table of the same type as the donor's breath weapon, or half as much damage on a successful save. The breath weapon's damage, save DC, and area of effect vary with the donor's {@variantrule Challenge Rating|XPHB}, as shown on the Draconis Fundamentum table.

Once you activate this graft, you can't do so again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. You can also restore your use of it by expending a number of {@variantrule Hit Point Dice|XPHB} as shown on the Draconis Fundamentum table (no action required).

name: Encyclopedia Sanguine
entries: This book catalogs many hundreds of bloody ink blots. While holding the book, you can cast {@spell Blood Print|ValdaSpire24} from it. If you consult the book as a {@action Magic|XPHB} action, you can determine the following about any such print: the specific kind of creature to which the blood belongs (such as a human or a unicorn), its approximate age, sex, and its health (assessed as poor or healthy).

name: Fate Deck
entries: This box of cards is interwoven with the threads of fate. A full deck contains a set of 52 {@item playing cards|XPHB}, but other variations exist, including those with different numbers of cards and sets of dice.
Playing any game with the deck casts {@spell Game of Fate|ValdaSpire24} (DC 17) from it. The deck can't cast this spell again until the next dawn.

name: Grimoire Monstrum
entries: While holding this book of myths and monsters, you have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Intelligence checks you make related to monsters, spells, or secret or ancient lore.

name: Heart of Steel
entries: {@i Donor: Any Construct}

This Construct core acts as a replacement for one's heart. Once installed, you don't need to sleep, and magic can't put you to sleep. You can finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB} in 4 hours if you spend those hours in a motionless state, during which you retain consciousness.

name: Heavy Legs
entries: {@i Donor: Large or Larger Monstrosity}

Once these legs are installed, you can use your {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to kick a creature of Large size or smaller within 5 feet of you. Make an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB}. On a hit, the target takes no damage but is pushed 5 feet away from you.
You also count as one size larger when determining your carrying capacity.

name: Hellfire Blood
entries: {@i Donor: Any Fiend}

When you take damage from a creature you can see within 30 feet of yourself, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} and expend a {@variantrule Hit Point Dice|XPHB|Hit Point Die} to throw vengeful hellfire. The creature that damaged you takes Fire damage equal to one roll of the {@variantrule Hit Point Dice|XPHB|Hit Point Die} plus your Constitution modifier.

name: Hunting Trap
entries: As a {@action Utilize|XPHB} action, you can set a Hunting Trap, which is a sawtooth steel ring that snaps shut when a creature steps on a pressure plate in the center. The trap is affixed by a heavy chain to an immobile object, such as a tree or a spike driven into the ground. A creature that steps on the plate must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw or take {@damage 1d4} Piercing damage and have its {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} reduced to 0 until the start of its next turn. Thereafter, until the creature breaks free of the trap, its movement is limited by the length of the chain (typically 3 feet). A creature can use its action to make a Strength ({@skill Athletics|XPHB}) check against your Traps save DC, freeing itself or another creature within its reach on a success. Each failed check deals 1 Piercing damage to the trapped creature. It takes a {@action Utilize|XPHB} action to recover the Hunting Trap.

name: Razor Wire
entries: As a {@action Utilize|XPHB} action, you deploy a tangle of Razor Wire. The wire occupies up to four 5-foot {@variantrule Cube [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Cubes}, each of which must be contiguous with at least one other {@variantrule Cube [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Cube} and be in an unoccupied space on the ground within 10 feet of you. The area of the Cubes is {@variantrule Difficult Terrain|XPHB}. When a creature moves into or within the area, it takes {@damage 1d4} Slashing damage for every 5 feet it travels. Razor Wire can't be recovered once deployed.

name: Trigger Bomb
entries: As a {@action Utilize|XPHB} action, you toss this explosive device into an unoccupied space within 30 feet of you. When a creature moves within 5 feet of the Trigger Bomb, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to press a detonator and cause it to explode in a 5-foot {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation}. Each creature within {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} makes a Dexterity saving throw, taking {@damage 1d6} Fire damage on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful one. Flammable objects in the {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} that aren't being worn or carried start {@hazard Burning|XPHB}, and Trigger Bombs within the {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} instantly detonate. A creature makes a save from a Trigger Bomb only once per turn. It takes a {@action Utilize|XPHB} action to recover the Trigger Bomb.

name: Leaping Legs
entries: {@i Donor: Any Creature with the Standing Leap Trait or Leap Bonus Action}
You can take a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to jump up to 15 feet by spending 5 feet of movement.

name: Legendary Trophy
entries: {@i Donor: Any Creature with Legendary Actions}
You can take a {@action Magic|XPHB} action to display this trophy-graft and give yourself and each of your allies within 30 feet of yourself {@variantrule Heroic Inspiration|XPHB}.
Once you activate this graft, you can't do so again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

name: Mechanical Limb
entries: {@i Donor: Any Medium or Larger Construct}

This additional arm installs beneath your normal arms. This arm can be used to hold weapons and Shields (allowing you to simultaneously hold a two-handed weapon and a one-handed weapon), perform Somatic components of spells, and perform other actions, though the arm doesn't grant you additional actions.

name: Monstrous Bite
entries: {@i Donor: Any Creature with a Bite Action}

This graft attaches the teeth of a monster onto your jaws. You can use your Dexterity modifier instead of your Strength modifier for the attack and damage rolls of your {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB|Unarmed Strikes}. When you deal damage with an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB}, you can deal Piercing damage equal to {@dice 1d6} plus your Strength or Dexterity modifier instead of the strike's normal damage. When you score a {@variantrule Critical Hit|XPHB} with a melee attack, you can make an attack with your Monstrous Bite as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}.

name: Monstrous Hide
entries: {@i Donor: Any Creature with AC 17+ Without Armor}

Your base {@variantrule Armor Class|XPHB} equals 13 plus your Dexterity modifier. You can wear armor on top of your Monstrous Hide, and you can use either armor to determine your AC. You can use a Shield and still gain this benefit.

name: Monstrous Weapon
entries: {@i Donor: Any Creature with a Claw or Rend Action}

This graft attaches a monster's prominent claws onto your hands. You can use your Dexterity modifier instead of your Strength modifier for the attack and damage rolls of your {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB|Unarmed Strikes}. When you deal damage with an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB}, you can deal Slashing damage as shown on the Monstrous Weapon table plus your Strength or Dexterity modifier instead of the strike's normal damage.

name: Nocturnal Eyes
entries: {@i Donor: Any Creature with {@sense Darkvision|XPHB}}
These eyes can see in the dark. Once installed, you gain {@sense Darkvision|XPHB} with a range of 60 feet.

name: Ooze Infusion
entries: {@i Donor: Any Ooze}
This graft causes your internal anatomy to become semi-fluid. Any {@variantrule Critical Hit|XPHB} against you becomes a normal hit.

name: Oversized Arms
entries: {@i Donor: Any Giant}
Once this graft is installed, your reach is 5 feet greater whenever you make an attack with a Melee weapon or {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB}.

name: Prehensile Tail
entries: {@i Donor: Any Creature with a Tail}
This graft attaches a flexible tail to your body. You can hold and manipulate objects and weapons with your tail, but you can't make attacks with it and it can't hold a Shield.

name: Regenerating Marrow
entries: {@i Donor: Any Creature with the Regeneration Trait}

If you are {@status Bloodied|XPHB} and have at least 1 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point}, you can take a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} and expend one of your {@variantrule Hit Point Dice|XPHB}, roll the die, and regain a number of {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} equal to the roll plus your Constitution modifier (no action required).

name: Replacement
entries: {@i Donor: Any Donor}

This graft replaces an organ or limb. A Replacement can replace an amputated limb or missing organ but can't revive a creature that has died. A Replacement organ or limb takes up one body slot relevant to it; for example, a monstrous hand takes the Arms slot and a Replacement kidney takes up the Internal slot. You can have more than one Replacement in a single body slot.

name: Resistance Suture
entries: {@i Donor: Any Creature with {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to Acid, Cold, Fire, Lightning, Poison, or Thunder Damage}
You have {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to one of the following damage types to which the donor had {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB}: Acid, Cold, Fire, Lightning, Poison, or Thunder.

name: Shapeshifter Blood
entries: {@i Donor: Any Creature with the Shape-Shift Action or Bonus Action}

You can shape-shift over the course of 1 minute to perfectly alter your appearance. You decide what you look like, including your height, weight, facial features, sound of your voice, hair length, coloration, and other distinguishing characteristics. You can make yourself appear as a member of another species, though none of your statistics change. You can't appear as a creature of a different size, and your basic shape stays the same.

name: Sprinting Legs
entries: {@i Donor: Any Creature with Speed of 60+ feet}
While this graft is attached, your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} increases by 10 feet and {@action Opportunity Attack|XPHB|Opportunity Attacks} have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} against you.

name: Frog Prince Statuette
entries: While holding this clay statuette of a frog, you can speak its command word and kiss it to cast the spell {@spell Mandy's Feral Follower|ValdaPlayerPack}, transforming the statuette into a {@creature Commoner|XMM}. The commoner created by the statuette retains the memories of each time it is transformed, no matter what appearance you ascribe to it.
Once it has been used, the statuette can't transform again until the next dawn.

name: Leonora's Throne of Indolence
entries: This high-backed armchair made of oak and gold weighs 100 pounds. When you sit in it and speak its command word as a {@action Magic|XPHB} action, it hovers beneath you and can fly through the air. The throne has a {@variantrule Fly Speed|XPHB} of 50 feet, can hover, and can carry up to 400 pounds. The throne stops hovering when you speak its command word again.
By speaking a second command word, you can cast {@spell Unseen Servant|XPHB} using the throne. The servant can conjure a spectral trumpet to announce your arrival, in addition to its usual tasks.

Lastly, you can speak a third command word as a {@action Magic|XPHB} action to magically create up to 10 pounds of delicious food of your choice and up to four bottles of wine. Only you can partake of this meal and drink; it instantly becomes stale and sickening in another creature's mouth. Once you have spoken this third command word, you can't do so again until the next dawn.

name: Memento Mori
entries: This sealed letter, infused with Chronomancy magic, contains a written description of how the creature that reads it shall die. The letter always contains specific descriptions, such as "The red-eyed orc drove its blade through Faizon the Blue's heart," but may also use cryptic or vague language. It never specifies an exact time. Once a creature has read the letter, it has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Death Saving Throws, and dies only after gaining five {@variantrule Death Saving Throw|XPHB} failures, instead of three. However, when the creature arrives at the moment of its death described in the letter, it dies without making Death Saving Throws if it is reduced to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}.
Once a Memento Mori is opened and read, it becomes an ordinary letter. Its effects end only if the creature that read it dies and is later restored to life.

name: Portable Cannonballs
entries: This bag contains twenty iron balls, each measuring one inch in diameter and weighing 1/4 of a pound. When poured out of their bag as a {@action Utilize|XPHB} action, the balls function as {@item Ball Bearings|XPHB}.

As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can speak the command word, which causes a number of the balls that you choose to expand into full-size cannonballs weighing 10 pounds each, suitable for firing from a cannon. A creature in the path of one or more cannonballs rolling downhill must succeed on a DC 13 Dexterity saving throw or take {@damage 2d10} Bludgeoning damage and have the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition if it is Large or smaller.

Each iron ball can also be used as a {@item Sling Bullet|XPHB} or a {@item Firearm Bullet|XPHB}. As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} when you make an attack with an iron ball as ammunition, you can expand it in midair. On a hit, this attack deals Bludgeoning damage equal to {@dice 2d12} plus the ability modifier used for the attack roll instead of the weapon's normal damage.

name: Ring of Barrels
entries: This ring has 6 charges and regains {@dice 1d6} expended charges daily at dawn. While wearing the ring, you can take a {@action Magic|XPHB} action and expend 1-3 charges to summon a number of empty Barrels in spaces within 5 feet of you equal to the number of charges expended. A Barrel provides {@variantrule Cover|XPHB|Half Cover} to a Medium or smaller target behind it and can be moved or set to rolling with a {@action Utilize|XPHB} action. A Barrel has AC 15 and 20 HP.

If you summon a Barrel into a space occupied by a Medium or smaller creature, the creature must succeed on a DC 13 Dexterity saving throw to be trapped within the Barrel. It has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on its saving throw unless its {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} is 0. A Medium creature trapped within a Barrel has the {@condition Restrained|XPHB} condition, whereas a Small or smaller creature has {@variantrule Cover|XPHB|Total Cover} from effects outside the Barrel. Bursting free of the Barrel requires a successful DC 20 Strength ({@skill Athletics|XPHB}) check as an action.
